translationRepairs: Think of Ji Shao guarding the emperor's carriage in peril, Bian Kun falling to blades and shafts, Huan Xiong matching Tian Shu in devotion, Zhou Qi outdoing Jie Yang in steadfastness, Luo Ding dying for a former sovereign, Xin Ji refusing to bow to alien rulers, Zhang Yi drinking poison to keep his honor, Wang Liang cutting off an arm to prove his loyalty—each will like autumn frost, each spirit bright as noon, enough to quicken moral clarity for ages and shame a degenerate age.

Think of Ji Shao guarding the emperor's carriage in peril, Bian Kun falling to blades and shafts, Huan Xiong matching Tian Shu in devotion, Zhou Qi outdoing Jie Yang in steadfastness, Luo and Ding dying for a former sovereign, Xin and Ji refusing to bow to alien rulers, Zhang Yi drinking poison to keep his honor, Wang Liang cutting off an arm to prove his loyalty—each will like autumn frost, each spirit bright as noon, enough to quicken moral clarity for ages and shame a degenerate age.

羅丁 and 辛吉 each pair the surnames of two different men (Luo Qisheng and Ding Mu; Xin Mian and Ji Yi), parallel to the pairs that precede; literal error: rendered as two single persons "Luo Ding" and "Xin Ji".
Ji Shao, whose courtesy name was Yanzu, was the son of Ji Kang, who had served Wei as Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary.
Ji Shao, whose courtesy name was Yanzu, was the son of Ji Kang, who had served Wei as Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
中散大夫 is Grand Master of Palace Leisure (Ji Kang's famous title); literal error: rendered as "Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary", which is a different office.
So Zheng, punishing Duke You of Lu's rebellion, split minister Zijia's coffin open with an axe.
So Zheng, punishing the disorder against Duke You, split open the coffin of minister Zijia with an axe.
鄭討幽公之亂 refers to the murder of Duke You (Ling) of Zheng, avenged by Zheng on Zijia; literal error: Duke You is wrongly made a duke of Lu and the instigator of a rebellion.
Lu executed Guan Yin for his crime, and the Spring and Autumn closes by censuring Hui.
Lu punished the crime against Duke Yin, and the Spring and Autumn closes by censuring Hui.
魯戮隱罪 refers to the crime of murdering Duke Yin of Lu; literal error: 隱 is rendered as a person "Guan Yin" executed for a crime.
Prince of Changsha Sima Yi appointed him recorder-in-chief to the chief commander and Gentleman of the Secretariat.
Prince of Changsha Sima Yi appointed him Recorder-in-Chief to the General of Agile Cavalry and Gentleman of the Secretariat.
驃騎記室督 is the recorder-in-chief on the staff of the General of Agile Cavalry (驃騎); literal error: 驃騎 rendered as "the chief commander".
He began as Ye Province's chief clerk; when Prince of Qi Sima Jiong served as Grand Marshal, Bao became his chief clerk.
He began as Yu Province's chief clerk; when Prince of Qi Sima Jiong served as Grand Marshal, Bao became his chief clerk.
豫州 is Yu Province; literal error: rendered as "Ye Province".

Jiong spurned Bao's advice and took Yi's bait, memorializing: "Your servant burns as traitors overturn heaven; with Chengdu, Changsha, and Xinyue I raised righteous armies to heal the altars—my vow night and day is to exhaust myself for the throne alongside true kinsmen—may the spirits witness me.

Jiong spurned Bao's advice and took Yi's bait, memorializing: "Your servant burns as traitors overturn heaven; with Chengdu, Changsha, and Xinye I raised righteous armies to heal the altars—my vow night and day is to exhaust myself for the throne alongside true kinsmen—may the spirits witness me.
新野 is Xinye, the fief of the Prince of Xinye named in s0157; literal error: misspelled "Xinyue".
Months of siege reduced the court—about to surrender in person, the emperor groaned: "Qu Yun and Suo Jing misled me."
Months of siege reduced the court—about to surrender in person, the emperor groaned: "Qu Yun and Suo Chen misled me."
索 here is Suo Chen (索綝), chief minister of Emperor Min; literal error: rendered as a non-existent "Suo Jing".

Minister over the Masses Wang Hun took him as aide, then named him magistrate of Nanwuyang.
司徒 is Minister over the Masses; literal error: rendered as "Minister of Works" (司空).

州主簿 is the provincial registrar and 別駕 the Attendant Officer; literal error: 別駕 rendered as "chief clerk", the term used elsewhere for 主簿.

After Fu Jian took Liangzhou and Yizhou, Huan Huo named him Weixing prefect and later Jinchang.

The source dates this to the start of Emperor Xiaowu's reign (孝武帝初) and includes the rank 輕車將軍; literal error: the rendering omits both.

Wang Pou withdrew to perfect filial piety; Ji Shao gave himself for the realm—orchid and laurel, different wood but shared perfume—like Shao music and Wu dance, distinct yet equally fine.

Ji Shao died to keep his integrity whole—that was his path.
